record_type_quote: We replicated their findings by retrospectively examining renewal across various topographies of automatically maintained behavior treated at an inpatient hospital, and we extended their work by also examining differences across subtypes of automatically maintained self-injurious behavior.

targets.authors: Muething C, Call N, Ritchey CM, Pavlov A, Bernstein AM, & Podlesnik CA
targets.title: Prevalence of relapse of automatically maintained behavior resulting from context changes.
targets.evidence_quote: Replication and extension of the lone CCCS focusing on the renewal of automatically maintained challenging behavior with a different clinical sample and setting is a logical and necessary next step in this line of research. Doing so would help to identify and establish the boundaries of generality with respect to the prefatory findings of Muething et al. (2022) as well as set the stage for additional investigations on factors that may influence renewal and ways to mitigate renewal of automatically maintained challenging behavior.
targets.outcome_quote: We replicated the findings of Muething et al. (2022) , thereby further establishing the scope and characteristics, generality, and believability of renewal as they relate to automatically maintained behavior (see Hagopian, 2020 ).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall concluding verdict states that the findings were replicated. Differences in postchange assessment and subtype extensions do not override this verdict.

reasoning: A new inpatient sample re-tests the outpatient renewal findings of Muething et al. (2022). Prior renewal series and subtype classification studies supply background or methods rather than separate targeted replications.
